commits.edited_message:
liblzma: Index decoder: Detect a too large allocation earlier

Previously, if an Index had more than PREALLOC_MAX Records, then allocations were done in PREALLOC_DEFAULT chunks (512 Records). That makes little sense in practice because it is likely that one would run out of address space later. Return LZMA_MEM_ERROR error pre-emptively if PREALLOC_MAX would be exceeded.

Also store the exact Record count in lzma_index_prealloc() and let lzma_index_append() apply the default group size when needed.

liblzma: index.c 1/4: Add bias members

In this commit the biases are still constant.

Also simplify Record group allocation by using the preallocated Record count directly.

coupling: The first edited commit makes lzma_index_prealloc() store the exact Record count, including zero, and moves the default-size handling into lzma_index_append(). That commit is safe by itself. The later edited commit simplifies lzma_index_append() to consume i->prealloc directly. With the original prealloc behavior, zero is never stored, so the later commit is also safe by itself. Their composition leaves i->prealloc == 0 after decoding an empty Index; the subsequent public lzma_index_append() allocates sizeof(index_group) with a zero-length flexible array and writes records[0]. The producer and consumer of the nonzero-prealloc invariant are in different commits, so a reviewer must inspect both maintenance changes to restore the invariant coherently rather than reasoning from either diff in isolation.
